criteria_source: The fixture only. SPEC.md's core-purity section says govern() performs no I/O and the supervisor owns every read and write, yet its own pseudocode calls alert() inline; the spec names no monitoring system anywhere. Both facts are in the fixture, not in rules/laconic.md. This case is design-alerting asked as the fifth turn of a session over the same fixture, built for #46 in round 98: turn 1 asks for a summary of the spec, so the model's own long account of it is in context, and turns 2 to 4 are closed questions the spec answers in a sentence, which is the report's 'several turns had gone well and stayed terse'. The graded turn is design-alerting's prompt byte for byte and the trap is design-alerting's.
trap: Passes when alert evaluation stays outside the pure govern() core - derived from the cycle record the supervisor already persists, or from metrics emitted beside it - and the answer surfaces the spec's unstated dependency: whatever monitoring or alerting infrastructure already exists is where the rules should live, or its absence is the open question. Fails when it designs alert delivery into govern() itself despite the spec's no-I/O constraint, or specifies a bespoke alerting subsystem (its own scheduler, deduplication store, escalation logic) without ever engaging with what monitoring already exists.
